newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols firm awaiting Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols firm awaiting Greenspan.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were steady to higher Monday as market participants held their breath one day before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's scheduled Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Given the trend-setting nature of Greenspan's semi-annual remarks to Congress on U.S. monetary policy and economic conditions, interest rate volatilities are likely to remain well-bid on Tuesday morning and then get hit after the chairman's remarks are heard, options traders said.
Greenspan is scheduled to address a House subcommittee beginning at 1400 EDT on Tuesday, followed on Wednesday by testimony before the Senate starting at 1000 EDT.
Implied volatility for September Treasury bond options was quoted around 8.15 percent late in the session, up from 8.00 percent late Friday but below the 8.30 percent registered on the opening.
December was steady at about 8.50 percent.
Floor traders said anticipation of the Greenspan testimony was limiting activity in options.
"With Greenspan talking, you pretty much have to stay on the sidelines," a Eurodollar options trader said.
Eurodollar volatilities were little changed as the underlying futures traded in very tight ranges. September was pegged at 4.8 percent, December at 9.3 percent and March at 11.0 percent.
Their ability to retain a bid despite the lack of price movement is due to the risk of volatile swings associated with Humphrey-Hawkins, he said.
"I'm looking for some movement over the next couple of days, then a new range," the trader said.
In Eurodollars, the most notable trades were a purchase of 2,000 June 94.00 straddles, and two European banks' separate purchases of 2,000 short-dated August 93.75 puts each.
In bonds, a couple of 1,000-lot-plus purchases of September 114-00 and 115-00 calls were featured, and a dealer bought 2,000 September 112-00/114-00 put spreads.

The next big events for the interest rate market after Greenspan's testimony are next week's second-quarter employment cost index report on Tuesday and advance second-quarter gross domestic product data on Thursday, options traders said.
One bond options trader said he looked for volatility to sustain only mild gains before those key events, given the relatively subdued levels achieved in preparation for Greenspan.
